column3: NASB renders “opposite” as “on the other side.”
NASB follows the critical text; “came to him” is rendered “came upon him.”
NASB adds “on them”; “bound up” is rendered “bandaged up.”
NASB follows the critical text; “seems to you to have been” is rendered “do you think proved to be.”
NASB follows the critical text; “compassion” is rendered “mercy,” and “act likewise” is “do the same.”
NASB follows the critical text without “into her house,” yet adds “into her home”; “received” is rendered “welcomed.”
NASB follows the critical text (“the Lord’s feet”).
NASB adds “all” and “to do all”; “service” is rendered “preparations.”
NASB follows the critical text; “anxious” is rendered “worried,” and it adds “so.”
NASB follows the critical text (“one thing is necessary”); “portion” is rendered “part.”
